flags.finding: [partially supported] The soundtrack playback of 'California Love' (written by Tupac Shakur and Andre Young / Dr. Dre) in S152 requires a music synchronization license for the underlying composition. As established under standard music licensing guidelines, synchronization clearance must be obtained directly from the copyright owners and music publishers controlling the composition. Because multiple writers and samples are embedded in the work, co-publisher splits must be verified via Songview prior to licensing. For an indie feature, commercial sync fees for a major hip-hop anthem are substantial ($25,000–$60,000); the production should maintain a production-library cue or indie alternative in post-production if quotes exceed budget.

citations.title: ASCAP's Articles and Advice FAQ: How To Acquire Music For Films
citations.excerpt: Synchronization License: This is the right to synchronize a song or a piece of music with your visual image. It must be obtained from the copyright owner of the music, which is usually the publisher.

remedy.detail: Negotiate a synchronization license from the publishers controlling the composition (confirm splits across co-writers via Songview; estimated licensing cost $25,000–$60,000). Temp/placeholder during the edit, and prepare an indie hip-hop production library replacement if commercial sync quotes exceed budget.

flags.finding: The featured on-screen display of four postwar and contemporary art paintings on Mark's laptop screen in S148 requires visual art copyright clearance. Under Ringgold v. Black Entertainment Television, Inc., 126 F.3d 70 (2d Cir. 1997), unauthorized reproduction and prominent display of copyrighted visual artworks in television and film productions constitutes copyright infringement rather than de minimis or fair use. Because postwar and contemporary artworks remain under copyright protection, the production cannot display identifiable real-world modern artworks without licenses from the copyright holders or representative organizations such as the Artists Rights Society, Inc. If specific paintings are not yet selected, the production can utilize public domain artworks (pre-1930) or commission original artist clearance graphics.

citations.title: 126 F3d 70 Ringgold v. Black Entertainment Television Inc | OpenJurist
citations.excerpt: The Court acknowledged that the second factor — nature of the copyrighted work — favored Ringgold in view of the imaginative nature of her artwork. ... ¶76 . The _amicus curiae_ brief for the Artists Rights Society, Inc. and the Picasso Administration strongly indicates evidence of licensing of artistic works for film and television set decoration, evidence that plaintiff is entitled to present at trial.

citations.title: Copyright & Artwork in Movies
citations.excerpt: producers of plays, films, and television programs should generally expect to pay a license fee when they conclude that a particular work of copyrighted art is an appropriate component of the decoration of a set.

remedy.detail: Select four specific artworks and obtain visual art licenses through the Artists Rights Society, Inc. or respective artist estates (licensing fees typically $500–$2,500 per artwork; $2,000–$10,000 total). Alternatively, populate the laptop display graphics with pre-1930 public domain fine art or original custom graphics created as works-for-hire by the production art department.

flags.finding: [partially supported] The prominent on-screen display of Counter-Strike gameplay on computer monitors in S161 requires an audiovisual copyright and trademark license from the game's publisher and copyright owner, Valve Corporation. Video game screen displays, animations, user interface elements, and accompanying audio are proprietary audiovisual works protected by copyright. Displaying identifiable gameplay on camera exceeds nominative mention and requires formal permission from Valve Corporation. Alternatively, the production art department can display fictional, royalty-free, or custom-built first-person shooter gameplay assets on the screens to avoid commercial licensing fees.

flags.finding: [partially supported] The explicit naming of real Harvard undergraduate Billy Olson in S006 as the person who suggested comparing female students to 'farm animals' presents acute defamation and false light exposure. Because Billy Olson is a private individual rather than a public figure, he is not required to prove actual malice under Gertz v. Robert Welch, Inc., but merely negligence, in a defamation action. flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S085 depicts an extended outdoor night hazing sequence in Harvard Yard during active snow and sub-freezing temperatures ('It’s snowing and cold as hell... most of whom are in their underwear with a couple of them wearing pants. They’re all blue and shivering... another kid simply falls to his hands and knees and throws up'). Staging actors and background performers outdoors at night in minimal clothing (underwear only) exposed to freezing conditions, wind chill, and wet snow poses severe risks of acute hypothermia, frostbite, and cold-induced nausea. Under CSATF Safety Bulletin #34 (Guidelines for Working in Extreme Cold Temperature Conditions), production must implement strict thermal protection protocols, including heated holding tents/trailers immediately adjacent to set, warm thermal robes/blankets and footwear provided between every take, hot fluids/nutrients, and strictly monitored duration limits for outdoor exposure.

citations.title: SAFETY BULLETIN #34 GUIDELINES FOR WORKING IN EXTREME COLD TEMPERATURE CONDITIONS
citations.excerpt: Preventing hypothermia is not difficult. In fact, it is much easier to avoid hypothermia than to treat it after the fact. You can prevent hypothermia if you pre-plan, know what the conditions are expected to be and plan your clothing accordingly.

citations.title: INDUSTRY DRIVERS! Guidelines for Working in Extreme Cold Temperature Conditions
citations.excerpt: Safety tips include dressing properly, providing your body with the appropriate nutrients and fluids, adequately securing equipment, and having emergency supplies readily available.

remedy.detail: Provide heated cast holding trailers/tents immediately adjacent to the set location, insulated footwear and heavy thermal parkas/blankets between all takes, hot beverages, and stage warm-air blowers on set perimeter (cost varies by region, est. $1,000–$4,000 for mobile heating gear and craft service warming supplies). Enforce strict exposure time limits (maximum 2–3 minutes of exposed takes before warming cycles) under the supervision of a production set medic to monitor for early symptoms of hypothermia. Use artificial visual snow / warm water mist if practical temperatures cannot be maintained.

flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S157 depicts live aerialists performing overhead inside a crowded nightclub ('hanging from the ceiling are two trapeze bars with two performers swinging and contorting' directly above a packed dance floor of 20-somethings). Under CSATF Safety Bulletin #4 (Stunts) and General Code of Safe Practices for Production, all overhead aerial acts require certified stunt rigging, load-rated and inspected structural anchor points, secondary safety fall-arrest lines or safety nets, and a designated clear floor perimeter directly below the swinging radius of the aerialists to protect ground personnel and background cast.
